contact_notices.description: The list of contact notices that the caller acknowledges. Possible value is PUBLIC_CONTACT_DATA_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

domain_name.description: Required. The domain name. Unicode domain names must be expressed in Punycode format.

domain_notices.description: The list of domain notices that you acknowledge. Possible value is HSTS_PRELOADED
domain_notices.rationale: Acknowledging HSTS preloading ensures that the domain is included in the HSTS preload list, which forces browsers to always use HTTPS, preventing SSL stripping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

labels.description:
Set of labels associated with the Registration.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Free-form key/value labels on the registration. Labels are cosmetic/metadata used for governance and cost tracking; per the rubric they are not a security control and constraining them offers no security gain.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

contact_settings.description: Required. Settings for contact information linked to the Registration.

contact_settings.privacy.description:
Required. Privacy setting for the contacts associated with the Registration.
Values are PUBLIC_CONTACT_DATA, PRIVATE_CONTACT_DATA, and REDACTED_CONTACT_DATA
contact_settings.privacy.rationale: Contact privacy (WHOIS protection) is essential to prevent personal data exposure and reduce the risk of spear-phishing and social engineering attacks against domain owners.

contact_settings.admin_contact.description:
Caution: Anyone with access to this email address, phone number, and/or postal address can take control of the domain.

Warning: For new Registrations, the registrant receives an email confirmation that they must complete within 15 days to
avoid domain suspension.

contact_settings.admin_contact.email.description: Required. Email address of the contact.

contact_settings.admin_contact.fax_numbe.description: Fax number of the contact in international format. For example, "+1-800-555-0123".

contact_settings.admin_contact.phone_num.description: Required. Phone number of the contact in international format. For example, "+1-800-555-0123".

contact_settings.admin_contact.postal_ad.description: Required. Postal address of the contact.

Unstructured address lines describing the lower levels of an address.
Because values in addressLines do not have type information and may sometimes contain multiple values in a single
field (e.g. "Austin, TX"), it is important that the line order is clear. The order of address lines should be
"envelope order" for the country/region of the address. In places where this can vary (e.g. Japan), address_language
is used to make it explicit (e.g. "ja" for large-to-small ordering and "ja-Latn" or "en" for small-to-large). This way,
the most specific line of an address can be selected based on the language.

Highest administrative subdivision which is used for postal addresses of a country or region. For example, this can be a state,
a province, an oblast, or a prefecture. Specifically, for Spain this is the province and not the autonomous community
(e.g. "Barcelona" and not "Catalonia"). Many countries don't use an administrative area in postal addresses. E.g. in Switzerland
this should be left unpopulated.

Generally refers to the city/town portion of the address. Examples: US city, IT comune, UK post town. In regions of the world
where localities are not well defined or do not fit into this structure well, leave locality empty and use addressLines.
The name of the organization at the address.

Postal code of the address. Not all countries use or require postal codes to be present, but where they are used,
they may trigger additional validation with other parts of the address (e.g. state/zip validation in the U.S.A.).

The recipient at the address. This field may, under certain circumstances, contain multiline information. For example,
it might contain "care of" information.

Required. CLDR region code of the country/region of the address. This is never inferred and it is up to the user to
ensure the value is correct. See https://cldr.unicode.org/ and
https://www.unicode.org/cldr/charts/30/supplemental/territory_information.html for details. Example: "CH" for Switzerland.

dns_settings.description: Settings controlling the DNS configuration of the Registration.

dns_settings.custom_dns.description: Configuration for an arbitrary DNS provider.

dns_settings.custom_dns.name_servers.description:
Required. A list of name servers that store the DNS zone for this domain. Each name server is a domain
name, with Unicode domain names expressed in Punycode format.
dns_settings.custom_dns.name_servers.rationale: The list of custom name servers hosting the domain's DNS zone. These are references to the team's chosen DNS providers; a generic policy cannot enumerate approved name servers without hardcoding specific hostnames, which is overreaching. DNS-integrity protections (DNSSEC) live on dedicated fields, not this reference list.

dns_settings.custom_dns.ds_records.description:
The list of DS records for this domain, which are used to enable DNSSEC. The domain's DNS provider can provide
the values to set here. If this field is empty, DNSSEC is disabled.

dns_settings.custom_dns.ds_records.algor.description: The algorithm used to generate the referenced DNSKEY.

dns_settings.custom_dns.ds_records.diges.description: The digest generated from the referenced DNSKEY.
The hash function used to generate the digest of the referenced DNSKEY.

dns_settings.custom_dns.ds_records.key_t.description: The key tag of the record. Must be set in range 0 -- 65535.

dns_settings.glue_records.description: The list of glue records for this Registration. Commonly empty.

dns_settings.glue_records.host_name.description: Required. Domain name of the host in Punycode format.

dns_settings.glue_records.ipv4_addresses.description:
List of IPv4 addresses corresponding to this host in the standard decimal format (e.g. 198.51.100.1).
At least one of ipv4_address and ipv6_address must be set.

dns_settings.glue_records.ipv6_addresses.description:
List of IPv4 addresses corresponding to this host in the standard decimal format (e.g. 198.51.100.1).
At least one of ipv4_address and ipv6_address must be set.

management_settings.description: Settings for management of the Registration, including renewal, billing, and transfer

management_settings.preferred_renewal_me.description:
The desired renewal method for this Registration. The actual renewalMethod is automatically updated to reflect this choice.
If unset or equal to RENEWAL_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED, the actual renewalMethod is treated as if it were set to AUTOMATIC_RENEWAL.
You cannot use RENEWAL_DISABLED during resource creation, and you can update the renewal status only when the Registration
resource has state ACTIVE or SUSPENDED.

When preferredRenewalMethod is set to AUTOMATIC_RENEWAL, the actual renewalMethod can be set to RENEWAL_DISABLED in case of
problems with the billing account or reported domain abuse. In such cases, check the issues field on the Registration. After
the problem is resolved, the renewalMethod is automatically updated to preferredRenewalMethod in a few hours.
management_settings.preferred_renewal_me.rationale: Automatic renewal ensures the domain remains active and owned by the organization, preventing service downtime or competitive domain acquisition due to expiration.

management_settings.transfer_lock_state.description: Controls whether the domain can be transferred to another registrar. Values are UNLOCKED or LOCKED.
management_settings.transfer_lock_state.rationale: Enabling transfer lock prevents unauthorized domain transfers, protecting the organization's online presence from domain hijacking.

yearly_price.description:
Required. Yearly price to register or renew the domain. The value that should be put here can be obtained from
registrations.retrieveRegisterParameters or registrations.searchDomains calls.

yearly_price.currency_code.description: The three-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217.
yearly_price.currency_code.rationale: ISO 4217 currency code for the domain's yearly price. This is a billing/financial setting with no security dimension; predictable billing is a cost-management concern, not a security archetype.

yearly_price.units.description: The whole units of the amount. For example if currencyCode is "USD", then 1 unit is one US dollar.
